text.p: Here are the highlights from Swiss newspapers on Thursday:
- The Swiss government plans to end Swissair's monopoly on flights by revising of air traffic regulations.

- The Swiss government intends to reduce the number of "seasonal workers" or foreigners who will be granted permission to work here from November 1997 to October 1998 to 90,000 from 113,000 due to the current economic situation.
- Watch manufacturer SMH reported a 5.8 percent rise in 1996 sales compared with 1995.
- Lucerne-based jewelry group Bucherer posted a 19 percent profit increase in 1996.
- Swiss media group Ringier's 1996 results were lacklustre due to the ongoing recession and internal restructuring measures. The group's profit margin was only 1.9 percent.
- Switzerland has chosen Edgar Bronfmann, President of the Jewish World Congress, to lead the new special fund for Holocaust victims. The fund so far totals 146 million Swiss francs.
- Textile machines builder Saurer Group posted sales of 557 million Swiss francs for the first four months of 1997.
- SMH announced it will launch two new watch lines. One is a low-priced waterproof watch called Lanco, to be produced in China, the other a higher priced line of watches designed by Calvin Klein.
- Berne consumer goods group Valora wants to concentrate on trade and service, and plans to raise sales to five billion Swiss francs by the year 2005.
- Zschokke, the second biggest building group in Switzerland after the newly established Batigroup, closed 1996 with a loss of 117 million Swiss francs. -- Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
